findings.title: Shared runtime-neutrality enforcement permits Node dependencies

evidence.note: The production shared project explicitly grants Node ambient types.
The runtime-neutrality policy blocks client/server frameworks and selected browser globals, but contains no equivalent Node builtin-import or Node-global restriction.

evidence.measurement: Pinned scan of 146 TypeScript files found Node/global usage only in two test-tier sentinels; none of the 73 production-like files matched node:, Buffer, process, NodeJS, __dirname, or __filename.
evidence.note: Production shared code is currently runtime-neutral, so enforcing the intended contract has no migration debt.
The current Node ambient consumer is test-only process.env wiring, which can remain under a test-specific configuration.

findings.problem: The shared package is described and linted as runtime-neutral, but enforcement is one-sided: browser dependencies fail while process, Buffer, node:fs, or another server-only dependency can compile and lint. A new contributor can therefore break browser portability without crossing an enforced package boundary.
findings.proposedDirection: Ban Node builtins and Node-only globals in production shared files while retaining Node types for test-only configurations or targeted sentinel exclusions. Preserve the existing browser and framework restrictions.

findings.title: Worktree provisioning is hard-wired to devcontainer credentials despite the root Compose setup

evidence.note: admin_url unconditionally requires the primary checkout's .devcontainer/.env and reads DATABASE_URL only from it.
The root setup already defines PostgreSQL credentials and development, test, and E2E URLs for localhost:8002.
The root Compose stack is a distinct supported database topology driven by the root .env.
The mandatory source uses the container-only db:5432 hostname, so the two env files are not safely interchangeable.

findings.problem: A contributor using the root Compose stack already has valid administration credentials, but worktree provisioning fails until a second devcontainer-specific env file exists. Copying that file mechanically can select the wrong hostname outside the container.
findings.proposedDirection: Give admin_url an explicit credential-source contract: prefer a dedicated worktree-admin URL override, retain .devcontainer/.env compatibility, and support the primary root .env when it is the active Compose topology. Validate the selected URL before writes and align banked documentation finding L07-017 with that precedence.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: CQ25-5 and related CQ25-62/CQ25-63 records cover state and file-layout seams in worktree-db.sh, not its exclusive credential-source assumption; this direction also avoids the broad decomposition refused by CQ25-125/CQ25-126.

findings.title: Add a preview/apply safety boundary to SRD backfills

evidence.note: Two database-writing backfills are exposed immediately beside read- and generation-oriented SRD commands.
The common runner connects to serverEnv.databaseUrl and immediately invokes the mutating callback without CLI options, target confirmation, or preview mode.
The spell backfill performs updateMany once per corpus row.
The monster backfill overwrites four persisted fields row by row.

findings.problem: Contributors and harness users cannot inspect the selected database and planned change counts before these commands begin writing. The current workaround is manual DATABASE_URL inspection plus an external backup, and a wrong environment becomes observable only after mutation starts.
findings.proposedDirection: Use the common runner to print a sanitized host/database target and require an explicit apply flag. Add dry-run summaries to both callbacks, with transaction semantics chosen separately where their rejection behavior permits all-or-nothing execution.

findings.title: Let lint-ratchet proposal previews evaluate third-party rules

evidence.note: Proposal summaries can represent only core or local source kinds.
The proposal engine already receives the binding containing the repository's third-party plugin allowlist.
Third-party rule IDs are rejected with an error that names a possible future --plugin option.
The dry-run command documents core/local support and explicitly defers third-party previews.
The workaround is to author the plugin allowlist and complete registry entry before existing third-party infrastructure can be exercised.

findings.problem: Contributors, harness users, and external adopters cannot use the proposal command to discover the scope and baseline cost of a third-party rule. Hand-authoring the allowlist, source shape, parser profile, and registry entry defeats the command's safe-preview purpose.
findings.proposedDirection: Add explicit plugin identity and parser-profile proposal options, validate them against the injected binding and allowlist, construct the existing third-party source shape, and emit a promotable third-party registry entry.

findings.title: Homebrew write validation loses its type correlation before editor reads

evidence.note: The shared registry correlates each homebrew type with a schema only during validation, then returns an erased record.
The persisted read contract exposes entry data as Record<string, unknown> rather than a type-correlated discriminated union.
The server validates type-specific data before persistence but does not preserve that correlation in its response contract.
Editor adapters consequently accept opaque persisted records at the registry boundary.

evidence.measurement: Pinned exact-signature search found eight production getDefault* adapters, excluding the monster editor, that accept data?: Record<string, unknown>.
evidence.note: The erased contract creates a repeated client-side decoding family rather than an isolated exception.
A representative adapter manually probes and converts unknown persisted fields into editor form state.

findings.problem: Shared knows the relationship between a homebrew discriminator and its data schema, and server writes enforce it, but reads discard that relationship. Each editor must rebuild a partial decoder from unknown records, making additions laborious and creating competing definitions of persisted shape across shared and client.
findings.proposedDirection: Expose a shared typed read adapter or discriminated persisted-entry union derived from the existing registry. Make each editor receive its correlated data type, migrate the eight adapters incrementally, and preserve the deliberately separate form-state coercions covered by existing constraints.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The landed client cluster correlates editor form state only after getDefault; eight remaining getters still receive opaque persisted records because the shared type-to-schema relationship stops at validation.

findings.title: Downstream packages keep semantic copies beside shared rule authorities

evidence.note: Generic RollMode is declared inside an attack-specific schema module.
Generic d20 rules must import the type from that attack-specific location.
The client independently re-declares and operates on the same three-value roll-mode union.
Shared exports MAX_SPELL_LEVEL.
Server spell-slot synchronization encodes the same maximum as a local literal 9.
Shared owns DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_SIZE_FT.
The client defines a separate DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_SIZE for the same default.
Shared defines the closed MONSTER_SPELL_FREQUENCIES vocabulary.
The client mirrors the frequency vocabulary and presentation order instead of consuming the authority.
CR-to-proficiency rules remain client-local while the adjacent CR-to-XP authority is imported from shared.

findings.problem: Shared exports several rule constants or closed vocabularies, yet server and client retain semantic copies or cannot discover the neutral type because it lives in an attack-specific module. These copies look harmless to a new contributor but can drift independently across package boundaries.
findings.proposedDirection: Move RollMode to a neutral d20 contract, import shared constants and frequency tuples directly, and move CR-to-proficiency alongside shared CR-to-XP rules. Add a narrow semantic-straggler check to the existing authority-consolidation workflow rather than introducing a general constants package.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The routed sweep identifies concrete semantic stragglers left after the authority-consolidation ruling: RollMode, maximum spell level, template size, monster spell frequencies, and CR proficiency. CQ25-115, CQ25-117, and CQ25-182 cover adjacent landed clusters but not these remaining consumers.

findings.title: Make combat history navigable through one paginated read model

evidence.note: EncounterDetail optionally carries an embedded logs array.
Every detail query nevertheless includes the complete combatLogs relation without a limit.
The mapper always serializes those logs into encounter detail.
The separate combat-log API defaults to 50 entries and supports a cursor.
The service returns an ascending page and nextCursor.
The client issues one listCombatLogs query and passes only that first page to the panel.
The panel renders the supplied page but exposes no continuation control.

findings.problem: DMs and players get two competing history paths: encounter detail pays to load the full history but the UI ignores it, while the visible panel stops after the API's first 50 ascending records despite receiving a next cursor. Long encounters therefore make later history unreachable through the panel.
findings.proposedDirection: Remove logs from EncounterDetail and its unbounded include, make listCombatLogs the sole read model, and give the panel an infinite-query or explicit load-more flow with a clearly chosen newest-versus-oldest initial-page policy.

findings.title: Turn the disabled stat-block placeholder into a party reveal workflow

evidence.note: The VTT contains a disabled stat-block action presented as a future capability.
Current token stat-block access is restricted to DMs.
Non-DM users are denied monster stat-block drawer access.
A reusable monster stat-block renderer already exists.
DM mutation controls are already isolated enough to omit from a spectator-safe rendering mode.
Encounter participant mutations already persist and broadcast participant state changes.

findings.problem: When a DM wants players to inspect a discovered creature, the current workaround is relaying selected statistics through chat or voice. Players cannot use the existing renderer because access is all-or-nothing and includes DM-only information and controls.
findings.proposedDirection: Persist an explicit per-participant reveal state, broadcast it through the existing encounter update path, and add a spectator-safe drawer mode that hides HP and mutation controls. Keep reveal distinct from ordinary token visibility so map information and rules information remain independently controllable.

findings.title: Let players choose Strength or Dexterity for Finesse attacks

evidence.note: The shared rule implementation silently chooses the better Strength or Dexterity modifier.
The seeded Finesse rule text states that the attacker chooses which ability to use.
The attack input contract has no ability-choice field.
The VTT dispatches weapon attacks without offering or sending that choice.

findings.problem: Players cannot exercise the explicit Finesse choice when both abilities are valid; the system silently optimizes instead. This matters for effects or table rules that distinguish the ability used, and the workaround is manual rolling outside the attack workflow.
findings.proposedDirection: Add an optional server-validated Strength-or-Dexterity override for Finesse weapons, retain the current best-modifier selection as the default, and show a compact selector only when both choices are legal.

findings.title: Expose the level-up history already returned with each character

evidence.note: Shared defines structured CharacterLevelChoice records with level and choice metadata.
Character detail already returns levelChoices.

evidence.measurement: Pinned search found zero non-test production TS/TSX consumers of levelChoices.
evidence.note: The transmitted history has no client presentation.
The sheet presents only the next level-up transaction, not prior choices.

findings.problem: Players and DMs must reconstruct prior class, subclass, feat, and ability choices from the current sheet or external notes even though structured choice history is already included in character detail.
findings.proposedDirection: Render a read-only level timeline grouped by level and resolved to human-readable class, subclass, feat, and ability labels. Treat rollback as a separate future design because the records do not presently capture a complete reversible mutation manifest.

bugsSideList.title: Upcast slot-damage validation caps only one increment rather than the maximum cast result
bugsSideList.whySuspectedBug: The schema accepts baseDice plus one perLevelDice increment at or below 100, but execution multiplies perLevelDice by every slot level above the base. A spell such as base 98d6 plus 2d6 per level can pass validation and later exceed the dice parser's 100-die limit.

bugsSideList.title: Character sheet AC can disagree with encounter combat AC
bugsSideList.whySuspectedBug: The sheet displays freshly computed equipment and class AC while encounter combat resolves character AC from persisted stats.ac.
